heroHeadline:
UAP Disclosure:
PURSUE Releases Sixth File Tranche (71 Files) Days After Pentagon Waives NDA Barriers for Whistleblowers
heroSubtitle: Tracking official government actions, congressional hearings, declassified documents, and institutional statements on Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena. Sept 18: the Department of War published PURSUE's sixth tranche of declassified UAP files — 71 records (67 DoD, 4 from Colorado law enforcement) including 2008-2012 AAWSAP Defense Intelligence Reference Documents on warp-drive and wormhole research, a declassified 1952 Tremonton, Utah film, and 2022-2025 infrared sensor footage — bringing the cumulative PURSUE total to roughly 450 files across six tranches. Sept 14: the Department of War issued a further legal waiver letting current and former personnel disclose UAP-related national defense information directly to PURSUE representatives without triggering NDA or Special Access Program agreement violations. These follow Sept 9's first House Task Force hearing on the topic, where Air Force veteran Dylan Borland accused AARO of 'a misrepresentation of the truth,' and Sept 2's move to contract access to the National UFO Historical Records Center's private pre-1990 archive. The Senate returned from recess Sept 14 with a narrow pre-midterm window to add the UAP Disclosure Act to its own FY2027 NDAA text. Next EO milestone: 300-day full-disclosure-or-justify deadline in late Nov/Dec 2026.
footerNote: This tracker documents official statements, legislative actions, and institutional processes related to UAP disclosure. It does not validate or endorse the claims contained within official testimonies. EDITORIAL NOTE: Events record that officials made specific claims — not that those claims are verified as factually true. All contested claims include opposing positions.
